page: Amazon Web Services x1.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered for extraordinarily large working sets. Running on the Xen hypervisor, it provides 128 dedicated vCPUs derived from 64 physical cores across Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processors operating at 2.3 GHz. The instance is defined by its massive 1,952 GB memory capacity, providing 15.25 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware provisions also include 3,840 GB of integrated local SSD ephemeral storage and a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps, while omitting dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results reflect the characteristics of a high-density, multi-socket Haswell-generation configuration. Single-core processing registers in the bottom decile for both stress-ng (730.57) and Geekbench (866.0), demonstrating constrained per-thread performance. Conversely, aggregate parallelism achieves a multi-core stress-ng result of 60,929.83. The platform demonstrates high memory throughput, recording 268.24 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 133.02 GB/sec in writes. Networking and memory subsystem capabilities also support 46.67 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 32.85 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

The architectural tradeoffs of the x1.32xlarge center on its resource distribution. Lacking modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, the platform is inefficient for machine learning token generation and heavy compute tasks. However, the substantial memory allocation combined with bundled high-capacity local SSD storage delivers cost and operational efficiency for architectures constrained by physical RAM limits rather than raw compute cycles. This configuration is positioned for large in-memory database deployments such as SAP HANA, massive distributed caching layers, and high-volume batch data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services x1.32xlarge is an enterprise memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for vast memory-resident computing. Powered by Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processors clocked at 2.3 GHz, it allocates 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores on the Xen hypervisor. The instance features a substantial 1,952 GB memory footprint, paired with 3,840 GB of local SSD storage and a 25 Gbps baseline network link, with no GPU hardware attached. Synthetic testing reveals modest single-thread metrics alongside robust multi-threaded throughput and notable memory performance, achieving uncached read bandwidth of 268.24 GB/sec and over 32 million Redis operations per second. Due to older instruction capabilities, compute-intensive and machine learning generation workloads encounter throughput limits. Consequently, the instance is engineered specifically for memory-bound operational demands, including enterprise in-memory databases, large caching clusters, and extensive analytical data pipelines.
